SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with dominant distribution (4,900+ stores), structural pricing power, and consistent operating leverage — Q2 2026 EPS grew +14.3% YoY on +7.5% revenue with stable 49.2% gross margins. The business trajectory is healthy: guidance was raised, FCF conversion hit 86.4%, and Protective & Marine is a secular growth vector. However, the stock is fairly valued at 31.6x PE (mid-range of 28–37x) with a 3.2% earnings yield below the 4.68% 10-year Treasury, creating a negative equity risk premium that limits re-rating potential. Balance sheet leverage is elevated (D/E 2.55x) and equity actually compressed QoQ from $4.43B to $3.85B — partly from the $1.5B shareholder returns — which amplifies ROE and P/B artificially. The Q2 beat and guidance raise provide a modest near-term catalyst, and falling oil prices ($85.15 vs $109.76) could support margins, but the valuation already prices in steady execution. Net: solid franchise, healthy trajectory, but limited margin of safety at current multiples in a 4.68% rate environment. Mildly positive.
